title: Conductor runbook: SLO-driven staged failover, operator quiet-mode, and automated partial rollback
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Implement a 'Conductor' runbook that links predictive SLO degradation signals to a staged multi-region failover sequence, operator 'quiet-mode' pager attenuation, and an automated partial rollback/traffic-shed action that preserves critical operations while minimizing operator noise. The goal is to reduce noisy pages during transient degradations and enable safe automated mitigations for well-understood failure modes.
background: We observed high on-call fatigue during short-lived tokenization and kernel-scheduling regressions that triggered full-region escalations. Existing circuit breakers and static pager thresholds either silence real incidents or generate noisy flapping. This initiative combines a predictive degradation detector, grading of remediation actions by impact, and an operator-in-the-loop silent mode to surface only actionable alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor service can consume SLO-degradation events (probabilistic score) and map to a 3-stage remediation plan
Operator 'quiet-mode' attenuates non-actionable pages for events below configured 'escalation attenuation score' while still opening a low-priority incident in the console
Automated partial rollback can be triggered with configurable pre-checks (canary success, KV cache consistency) and a documented abort path
Integration tests simulate transient and persistent degradations and verify pages suppressed for transient cases, escalations for persistent cases
Runbook doc published in Confluence with run-levels, decision trees, and links to playbooks and dashboards
implementation_plan: Add a Conductor microservice to inference-control plane that subscribes to SLO anomaly stream and health events
Define 'escalation attenuation score' combining SLO breach probability, page volatility, customer impact, and historical flakiness
Implement staged remediation actions: 1) soft-shed non-critical traffic & prefork routing, 2) route traffic to adjacent region with gradual ramp, 3) initiate partial rollback of last deploy batch
Expose operator 'quiet-mode' toggle in Console and as API for on-call to temporarily raise suppression thresholds with automatic expiry
Add audit logs and 'why-silenced' telemetry for each suppressed page for postmortem
Ship integration tests and a chaos harness (fault-injection for kernel scheduler and KV cache) to validate behavior
rollout_plan: Week 1: Merge Conductor service with feature-flag disabled; deploy to staging and run synthetic degradations
Week 2: Enable feature-flag for non-prod and runbook dry-run (no pages suppressed; incidents logged)
Week 3: Canary in one low-traffic region; allow operator quiet-mode but require manual approval for automated rollbacks
Week 4: Expand to three regions with automated rollbacks enabled for low-risk services; monitor error budgets and page volume
Week 6: Full rollout with dashboarding and runbook training for on-call
testing_plan: Unit tests for score calculation and gating logic
Integration tests for staged remediation in preprod with injected SLO breaches
Chaos experiments: CPU/GPU kernel latency spike, KV cache eviction, simulated inter-region latency
Observer-driven verification: assert pages suppressed for >70% of transient flaps and not suppressed for persistent breaches longer than 5 minutes
metrics_and_alerts: pager_volume_weekly: track reduction of low-priority pages (target 40% reduction)
time_to_first_ack: measure latency when quiet-mode suppresses pages (should not exceed baseline by >30s)
false_suppression_rate: percent of suppressed events that later escalated (target <5%)
partial_rollback_success_rate: percent succeed without data loss or cascading failures (target >=99%)
notes: We should align attenuation score parameters with SRE council recommendations before canary
Legal asked for audit trail retention policy; retention set to 90 days for suppressed pages initially
Consider exposing a per-customer opt-out for automated reroute when privacy or data residency applies
